verdictNote: HARDEN's three scanner items and OPC's High, Medium and two Low items are fixed as asked. One change is needed before the lease: the new published-history admission also admits rewinding main to an older published commit, which drops the held sidecar locally (a regression, reproduced). The origin/main spoof is real but no worse than the hooksPath bypass; name it in section 7.

items.evidence: Scratch repo: c1 (code), c2 (acquire, sidecar held), origin/main=c2. guardReferenceTransaction(old=c2, next=c1) returns ADMITTED at HEAD and is refused by the pre-fix module (dc15c5030^, run from scratch). The rule only asks whether next is ancestor-or-equal of origin/main, so `git reset --hard HEAD~N` or `update-ref refs/heads/main <older published>` on main is admitted. After that, guardCommit reads the sidecar from refs/heads/main (now absent/released), so scoped commits on main pass pre-commit, and later forward moves compare the same absent sidecar (raw===nextRaw) and are admitted too. Syncing back to origin still fails without force (merge/rebase onto held origin hit the borrower check), so the damage stays local. A pull never needs a move behind origin/main.
items.fix: Admit published history only for a forward move or the exact published tip: `next === published || (oldOid is zero or merge-base --is-ancestor oldOid nextOid)` together with `merge-base --is-ancestor nextOid published`. This adds one more read (merge-base is already a declared hook verb). Add the rewind case to the 'published main admission distinguishes ancestry...' unit test.

items.area: guardReferenceTransaction trust in refs/remotes/origin/main; docs/platform/git/spec.md section 7
items.evidence: Reproduced: `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main <scoped c3>`, then the main update c2->c3 is ADMITTED. The same update is refused while origin/main=c2, and by the pre-fix module. The shell front end ignores transactions that do not touch refs/heads/main, so writing the remote-tracking ref is never checked. This is a deliberate local act, as bad as `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null update-ref refs/heads/main X`, which the hooks never stopped. Section 7 already calls the lease convention plus typed doors, not enforcement. No sound local check exists: reflog and fetch provenance are locally writable too. Only a server-side check (ls-remote in the hook, or branch protection) would be sound, and that costs network access on every main move.
items.fix: Do not add code. Add one sentence to section 7 'Uncovered raw routes': the published-history exemption trusts the local refs/remotes/origin/main, so anyone who rewrites that ref (or disables core.hooksPath) bypasses the reference guard. Real protection needs server-side enforcement.

items.evidence: Any resolved literal git program (named, .call, Reflect.apply, array-slot callers) refuses configured-binary. Escapes are kept only when every resolved program value is external, there is no aliased export, and an escaping program parameter adds an unknown. The 4+2 new cases fail against `git show 6215e614f:scripts/git-one-door-scan.mjs` and pass at HEAD.

Requires non-empty observed verbs, all in READ_VERBS. update-ref, unresolved argv, a variable verb, a prefix spread and symbolic-ref with a spread are refused (10 cases, all red against the pre-fix scanner).

`export { g as alias }` and `export { g as default }` now refuse (4 cases, all red against the pre-fix scanner). `export { g as h } from` and `export const alias = g` in another module make the declaration stale, which fails closed.

items.area: scripts/git-one-door-scan.mjs findCallers re-export branch (~:1313) and section 17 text
items.evidence: Probe: declared wrapper `export function g(args){execFileSync('git',args)}` with a declared-tooling-exemption. A second module re-exports it (`export * as ns from './read.mjs'`, `export * from './read.mjs'`, or `import * as r ...; export const ns = r`) and a caller runs `reset --hard` through it. The scan stays green with 0 undeclared on both the new and the pre-fix scanner, so this is not a regression. findCallers claims to handle `export * from`, but returns early because the re-exporting module has no `export ... g` text of its own, and `export * as ns` does not match its regex. No declared wrapper is re-exported today (rg finds no `export * from` in src/scripts/bin/.githooks). It is the same class of hole as HARDEN item 3, and section 17 no longer names any open alias gap.
items.fix: In computeValueFlow, also treat as an escape any other module that has `export * (as x)? from '<wrapper module>'` or a namespace-import re-export for an exported wrapper, and add one probe case to the alias test. If that waits, put an explicit open-gap sentence back in section 17.

items.evidence: Verb checks for hook and tooling declarations now accept `['diff', ...extra]` as diff (probe accepted). Trailing operands can carry `--output=<file>` (a filesystem write) or `--ext-diff`. They cannot move a ref. Identity hashing is still strict. config, reflog and symbolic-ref with a spread stay unknown.
items.fix: Optional: section 17 should say tooling verbs are literal but trailing operands may not be. Or keep the strict parse for hook-read-context.

items.evidence: Probe: `for (const c of readConfig()['checks']) execFileSync(c, ['push','--force'])` with readConfig returning `{checks:['git']}` gives an unresolved site, and a configured-binary declaration on it is accepted (fixedGit only sees resolved literals). This rule existed before the change, and HARDEN's ask ('refuse a resolved literal git; keep escape refusal unless proven') is met. No configured-binary declarations remain.
items.fix: Optional, cheap: require programs.configured for every configured-binary declaration. A provable site auto-classifies anyway, so the declaration class would only ever cover unproven programs.

items.evidence: Scratch copy of shared-config-file/merge/worktree/goal-check: merge.mjs:958, :992 and worktree.mjs:146 auto-classify as configured-binary '(configuration file data)'. Replacing `return JSON.parse(raw)` with a literal `{invariantChecks:{commands:['git push --force']}, worktreeSetup:{commands:['git reset --hard']}}` turns all three into reported sites. bin/fgos.mjs takes the same readInvariantCheckCommands path, and the full-tree scan stays at 0 undeclared. Class counts on the real tree are identical to HARDEN's (configured-binary 92, tooling 19, hook 23 ...), so the evaluator widening reclassified exactly these five sites. The declarations' own owner-approved retireWhen ('the scanner proves parsed-config provenance') is met.
items.fix: This is within HARDEN's verdict, because the declarations retire by their own condition and the proof is part of the scanner diff HARDEN re-reviews. No separate OK is needed, but name the retirement and the computed-property evaluator change explicitly in the re-review request.

items.evidence: In a scratch sha256 repo, `git hash-object -t tree --stdin </dev/null` prints 6ef19b41...c5321, and `rev-parse --show-object-format` prints sha256. The sha1 id 4b825dc6... is the standard one. An unknown format throws, so the hook fails closed. The declaration verbs (9 + merge-base) are accepted by the scanner, which requires equality with the observed literal caller verbs. `node scripts/git-one-door-scan.mjs --root . --write-census` exits 0 with 0 undeclared, and `git status` stays clean, so the committed census matches.

Section 7 matches the code: deletion is checked before the published admission, an absent origin keeps the local policy, a read/ancestry error (status not 1) is rethrown and fails closed, and absent main uses the empty tree. Uncovered routes are listed. The 2026-10-22 line was moved verbatim from section 18 to section 7 history. The section 17 alias and tooling text matches, apart from S4 and S5.
